proposals.description: Create a source-qualified preparation identity with partial source-supported components. NBRC 1116, 1195, 1196 and 1200 and TOGO M2186, M2708 and M3181 explicitly use volume-dosed concentrated HCl reagent. This record denotes the qualitative source-described acid preparation, with variable or unspecified strength, not pure gaseous HCl or a certified commercial formulation. It preserves the source reagent boundary at UNDEFINED_MIXTURE granularity. NBRC 1200 prints 51.3 mL where NBRC 1195/1196 print 51.3 microlitres; these receiving-stock quantities remain unresolved and are not used to derive acid strength. Literal 25%, 32% and 35% are retained as source specifications, not normalized comparable fractions. The cited sources do not state a common percentage basis, carrier, grade or assay tolerance; the exact same-or-distinct preparation relation is unresolved. TOGO M2305/M2746 explicitly calls its 25% input concentrated, so that qualitative label does not exclude a numerical percentage. If comparable definitions and assay ranges were established, a real strength difference could be assessed; they are not established here. Before co-installing overlapping candidates, the coordinator must choose an explicit common bounded partial-material scope preserving every source context, or obtain comparable preparation/product evidence. No owner merge or arbitrary winner is selected.

proposals.description: JCM1270 explicitly weighs44g BD-Difco Columbia blood agar base, then separately adds water and sheep blood. Manufacturer manual distinguishes Difco44g/L base from BBL42.5g/L and EH39g/L variants. This source-qualified owner denotes the dry Difco input; it does not reuse MICRO536 whose definition transcribes the BBL formulation. Typical constituent names are retained without historical lot or dry-mass-ratio claims. Recovered manufacturer-authored BD Difco & BBL Manual, second edition 2009, printed p158 (PDF page170), hosted by NMSU. The approximate per-liter Difco table lists pancreatic digest of casein10g, Proteose Peptone No.3 5g, yeast extract5g, beef heart infusion from500g 3g, corn starch1g, sodium chloride5g and agar15g; the footnote allows adjustment/supplementation to meet performance criteria. It directs suspension of44g powder in1L purified water. Those are manufacturer preparation/formula statements, not dry-product mass fractions, final yield, or an identified historical JCM lot. The same page separately gives BBL42.5g (including13.5g agar, meat peptic digest and heart pancreatic digest) and DifcoEH39g (including12g agar and different nutrient inputs).
